item.title: Alvarium Cave
item.description:
About

Two meter drop into cave which is little awkward but not bad from people smaller than me. This leads to a belly crawl for about 5-7m that opens into a wide low chamber about 4m in diameter and 1.5m high. The entrance pool is large and water clear. Line leads in from ceiling a couple of metres into the pool.

The nearest you can get with a car is about 700m or so from the entrance and you will need to carry in your cylinders and equipment. Ideally just take 7L tanks and be prepared to drag them through the dirt so a bag and rope are recommended.

Why not consider the stunning Cabaret Cave for your next function or event. Originally used in the 1930’s to provide a secret dinner and dance location for Perth’s rich and famous.

item.title: Coombe Reserve
item.description:
About

Local wreck trail and cave training area. Cave line and poles installed, along with series of “shallow wrecks” (5-9m) close to shore with other wrecks in deeper water (22m)

Details

Identification

  • Source: Facebook

Cave and exploration data

  • Vertical access: No
  • Tourism potential: Medium
  • Disabled access potential: Medium
  • Goes to water: Yes

Diving data

  • Maximum depth: 22 m
  • Tidal: Yes

Additional Notes

(Post by Joseph Bicanic on 19-Nov-2023) I’ve set up a new pole trail at The Coombe which, when set up (line installed), mirrors the requirements for CDAA Cave and Advanced Cave Training Dives. This pole trail can also be used for Basic Cave Divers. I’m hoping this gets used and maintained so the poles have any growth removed so as to make is less likely for Divers to cut their hans on the growth. Shallowest pole is in 3 - 4 m depth in forward of the park bench (2 poles at the start - 1 at an angle) Last pole also has 2 pole, both upright. Max depth 8 - 9 m. All poles on this circuit have 50mm of orange tape almost at the top. Shallowest and Deepest poles are all orange. Others are mostly grey. Orange circles in pic indicate the poles. Green circles in pic indicate anchor points for lost line procedures. Orange curve is a restriction. I’ve placed this in the water for myself as well as anyone else wanting to practice the circuit. I’m hoping this gets a bit of use as this will reduce the build up of growth on the poles. Please help in maintain as follows: Take a scourer of some type to scrub off any growth on poles. If a pole comes out - use a weight etc to hammer it back in. If there is a problem - DM me so I can attend to it. Enjoy

item.title: Jingemia Cave
item.description:
Details

Identification

  • Feature type: Cave

Additional Notes

Jingemia Cave is a distinctive natural feature in a band of low rocky hills that extend between the towns of Carnamah and Moora. The hills are an outcropping of chert and other very old rock types that formed between 2.5 billion and 542 million years ago (mid Proterozoic era). Known as Noondine Chert, this geological formation is significant in the region for having unique plants that grow only in association with chert. The formation also influences an aquifer that supplies groundwater to local towns, and is a source of mineral silica, a vital component in many things used in our everyday lives.

item.title: Mimbi Caves
item.description:
About

From https://www.showcaves.com/english/au/caves/Mimbi.html

Official Website

The Mimbi Caves formed inside Devonian limestone and were a place of deep spiritual significance to the Gooniyandi people. The caves are guided by an indigenous Gooniyandi guide who tells stories from the time when local Aboriginal people inhabited this area. He retells dream time stories and other fascinating stories from more recent times. He shows bush medicine plants and artefacts, how tools were made and how colour for cave paintings was prepared. The cave has some cave paintings and also speleothems in the deeper part. The hills show steep karren, some parts look like a stone forest. After the tour there is traditional Billie Tea and damper, made the traditional way using native seeds, around the campfire. The guide shares a song or two on the guitar and tells the Gooniyandi Dreaming story of the Blue Tongue Lizard and the Mud Lark.

item.title: Slot Cave
item.description:
About

Slot cave is located on the Roe Plains close to Burnabbie Cave. There is a well defined track leading from the main track to the cave itself. The cave is a slot about 10m long and 1-1.5m at its widest. The drop is about 4m and you will need a ladder or ropes to enter. There are two dives here, the upstream and the downstream.

Upstream

The upstream is an advance cave dive but quite open.

item.title: Tommy Graham's Cave - 6N56
item.description:
About

About

The entrance to the cave is a large doline 50m in diameter. The obvious route into the doline leads to short cave below the Northwest cliff line.

The main cave has been described as a “wombat- sized hole” which is found in the Southeast end of the doline, about 3m down from the level of the plain. There is a visitor book on a rock shelf in the entrance. The way on is not obvious and goes through a rock squeeze at the end of the low entrance chamber.

item.description:
Details

Identification

  • Feature type: Cave
  • System name: Yonderup
  • Source: Explore Parks

Cave and exploration data

  • Tourism potential: Medium

Additional Notes

Yonderup Cave is one of the adventure caves that are available by booking only. Experience an underground wonderland full of natural cave decorations such as stalagmites, helictites, columns and shawls throughout this ‘stream cave’.

A popular place for birthday parties and team building exercises.

During the guided walk you will discover the cave’s history, geology and the ecosystem that lies within. Yonderup Cave’s constant temperature makes this tour a comfortable all-year-round experience.
